db_evidence.notes: Querying episodes for literal text '寅虎' returns matches only at the 50160-50190 and 66150-66180 windows (plus rolled-up 1h/3min/6h/video summaries that inherit those hits) -- i.e. only 2 of the 6 clue intervals are name-searchable. The entities table has a separate row per appearance with inconsistent naming across the 6 encounters: 30870 -> '虎-headed foe (tiger-headed armored enemy)', 37140 -> 'tiger-headed npc', 50160 -> '寅虎 (tiger-headed demon npc / smith)', 66150 -> 'monkey-like npc smith (寅虎)', 68850 -> 'tiger-headed boss (乌川 / 南虎)'. Raw 30sec episode captions at the 37166-37225 and 40414-40497 windows describe the boss generically as a 'bear-headed enemy' / 'large armored foe' / 'hulking bear-headed enemy' rather than tiger/寅虎, so keyword search on 'tiger'/'虎'/'寅虎' structurally cannot find those two windows; only a full linear time-range scan of the whole day timeline (which no rollout performed) or the entities table (which one rollout queried but did not act on for 37140s) could surface them.

root_causes: Fragmented/inconsistent entity naming across the 6 Yin Tiger encounters (different auto-generated labels each appearance: 宓虎, 虎-headed foe, tiger-headed npc, 寅虎, 乌川/南虎) breaks name-based semantic_search and run_sql keyword lookups, so at best only 2/6 windows are name-searchable directly.

Auto-generated 30sec episode captions at the 37166-37225 and 40414-40497 windows describe the recurring boss as a generic 'bear-headed'/'armored' enemy, never mentioning tiger or 寅虎, making those two encounters undiscoverable by any keyword or semantic query anchored on the boss's name.

None of the 5 rollouts performed an exhaustive linear scan of the whole day-timeline episodes table for the boss's occurrences; each anchored on whichever subset of windows its keyword/entity searches happened to surface, so counts varied 1/3/3/3/4 depending on how much of that subset was covered.
One rollout (rollout-2) did retrieve the entities row for the 37140s occurrence but never followed up with a targeted SQL/clip_qa check, so retrieved evidence went unused.
One rollout (rollout-3) restricted essentially all exploration to the final 68700-70500s window and never scanned earlier time ranges at all, producing the most severe undercount (1).
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly used clip_qa to visually confirm each window they did find as a genuine Yin Tiger challenge attempt vs. a distractor menu/scene.
Rollout-0 achieved the best partial recall (4/6) by supplementing failed keyword searches with manual episode time-window scans around each hint it obtained.
Every rollout correctly identified the 68850-69071 window as the final, successful challenge.
transferable_lessons: For counting questions about a recurring character/boss across a very long timeline, do not rely solely on name-based semantic_search/run_sql keyword matches -- auto-generated captions can label the same entity differently at each appearance (species/animal-head descriptors vary). Cross-check the entities table for all distinct row_ids that could plausibly be the same recurring character and follow up each one with a targeted time-window run_sql and clip_qa, even if the name string differs.

When only 2 of N expected occurrences are literally name-searchable, treat that as a strong signal to do a broader/coarser sweep (e.g. run_sql over 1h or 3min granularity episodes across the full day range, or semantic_search with generic terms like 'boss fight'/'challenge' rather than the specific name) instead of stopping once a plausible small set is found.

For 'how many times before finally X' counting questions, cross-validate the discovered count against the number of distinct semantic-search/entity hits before submitting -- if the agent found fewer than 4-5 distinct hint sources for a supposedly repeated event, that is itself evidence of incomplete retrieval.
Do not confine exploration to the time range near the final/decisive event; earlier occurrences of the same repeated pattern must be actively searched across the entire timeline, not assumed absent.
open_questions: Whether a full linear scan of all 1h/3min granularity episode summaries across the whole day timeline (not attempted by any rollout) would have been sufficient to surface all 6 windows, or whether the underlying captions at 37166-37225 and 40414-40497 are ambiguous enough (bear-headed vs tiger-headed) that even a human skimming captions would struggle to attribute them to Yin Tiger without watching the actual clip.

Whether the reference answer's '6 times' itself double-counts any menu-browsing/re-entry into the challenge screen as a separate 'challenge' versus a single continuous fight, which could not be fully verified without frame-level inspection of all 6 windows.
